complaints.solution: The customer complained that a few blocks were received with cracks. The issue was related to the initial stage of production when the machine was starting up. After production started the machine settings were adjusted and the issue was corrected. The labour should have inspected the blocks coming out of the machine and removed any blocks with visible cracks before they were sent for delivery. The customer has already used the blocks.

Damaged Quantity: Approximately 5–6 pieces During the inspection, a few pavers were found to be brittle and prone to crumbling. The reason is believed to be that these pavers were relatively dry, which may have occurred during the production start-up stage due to water adjustment at the beginning of production. In addition, loading and unloading activities may have contributed to some of the observed damage. A sample of the same paver product was subsequently tested at the Hidd Yard, and the compressive strength was found to comply with the applicable standards. Based on the test results, the customer was reassured and agreed to proceed with using the material. Conclusion: At this stage, no replacement is required, as the damaged quantity is very limited and the material has already been used by the customer without any reported issues.

complaints.details: Too much dust in D.W. sand
complaints.solution: The site was visited, and the customer reported that shell smaller than 2 mm were present in the sand, which was causing cracks in the plaster work. Action taken: 5 ton were replaced with new sand
complaints.recommendation: Plaster sand has been received from other suppliers.

complaints.solution: Our technician was present at site, and the slump was checked and accepted by the clinet as per the customer request (120 mm). This slump is requires proper vibration to ensure good compaction. The honeycombing observed is mainly due to insufficient vibration during casting, not the concrete itself.
complaints.recommendation: He should take steps from his side.
